paper.title_en: Fast computation of microscopic optical potentials: beyond existing capabilities
paper.abstract_en: A microscopic approach to optical potential calculations, based on the leading term in the spectator expansion of the optical potential operator and carried out in momentum space, has been successful in describing nucleon elastic scattering above 100 MeV. However, high computational cost precludes the inclusion of all physics relevant to scattering, such as the tensor part of the nucleon-nucleon (NN) amplitude, three-nucleon forces, multiple scattering and medium effects. Also, this approach does not provide any nucleon-nucleus scattering wave functions needed for reaction calculations. In this Letter, we develop a harmonic oscillator expansion version of this approach, which provides the same representation of optical potential both in momentum and coordinate spaces, accelerates calculations by two orders of magnitude, includes the missing tensor component of the NN scattering amplitude and is applicable to nuclei with any spin. Test calculations have been performed for several light nuclei whose densities were obtained in the No-Core Shell Model using a chiral Hamiltonian. We demonstrate convergence of this expansion and clarify the role of the tensor force, which manifests itself mainly in coupling between channels with different spin. Comparison to experimental data is presented for selected cases. The methodology could be extended for scattering of other projectiles (hadronic and pionic), small complex nuclei and hypernuclei. It also suggests a pathway for including more complicated physics into the scheme and extending it to lower energies. It could be also helpful in assessing the accuracy of upcoming scattering emulators.
